content.objective: To interface an 8255 Programmable Peripheral Interface (PPI) with an 8086 microprocessor kit to control an 8-bit LED traffic light sequence.
content.theory: The 8255 is a general-purpose programmable I/O device designed for use with Intel microprocessors. It consists of three 8-bit bidirectional I/O ports (Port A, Port B, Port C) configured through an internal Control Word Register.
procedure: Connect the 8255 PPI interface board to the 8086 trainer kit bus.
Initialize Port A as output by writing the control word 80H to the control register at address 06H.
Write an assembly program in MASM to output binary sequence 00000001B to 10000000B with a 500ms delay subroutine.
Execute the program and verify the sequential blinking of LEDs on Port A.
content.conclusion: The 8255 PPI was successfully configured in Mode 0. The output latch correctly maintained steady logic states between clock cycles.
